construct: Osteoid osteoma is a small benign bone-forming tumor with a vascular osteoid nidus and surrounding reactive sclerosis; high local prostaglandin production contributes to severe nocturnal pain that characteristically responds to NSAIDs.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: An adolescent with focal nocturnal bone pain rapidly relieved by an NSAID and a small cortical radiolucent nidus surrounded by sclerosis has osteoid osteoma.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Osteoblastoma shares osteoid histology but is usually larger, often spinal, and its pain is less characteristically NSAID-responsive. The small cortical nidus plus nocturnal NSAID-relieved pain uniquely favors osteoid osteoma.
